Building on earlier ReplaySSM work.
NVIDIA and the Dao AI Lab at Princeton University explore how caching SSM inputs speeds up decoding and supports low-precision state with less error accumulation.
Hybrid models interleave state-space model (SSM) layers with a few attention layers.
NVIDIA Nemotron 3, Qwen3.5 through Qwen3.8, Kimi-K3, and GLM-5.3-Flash are all built this way, with Mamba-2, Gated DeltaNet (GDN), or Kimi Delta Attention (KDA) as the SSM layer.
SSM layers are designed to make decoding fast: they use a fixed-size state in place of a key-value (KV) cache that grows with context length.
At serving batch sizes, however, the SSM layers, not attention, can be the latency bottleneck up to 100K tokens of context.
SSM layers also complicate two techniques that reliably speed up attention decoding: speculative decoding and quantization.

ReplaySSM makes SSM layers the fast part again. It represents the SSM state as a checkpoint plus a buffer of recent inputs. This separates output computation from state updates and addresses three challenges in current SSM decoding: state traffic, rollback for speculative decoding, and error accumulation in a quantized state.
ReplaySSM is joint work between NVIDIA and the Dao AI Lab at Princeton.
The paper, ReplaySSM: Cache SSM Inputs, Not State, details all three benefits and presents the full evaluation.
It is available on arXiv, with code on GitHub.
It is integrated into NVIDIA TensorRT-LLM, vLLM, and FlashInfer, and also runs in production in GLM-5.3-Flash and Kimi-K3.
